summary: Check guest-IOVA (vIOMMU) readiness: every guest DMA address site, QEMU 10.2.4 IOMMU APIs, the guest driver side; design the seam now; detect+refuse at realize

# Guest IOVA (vIOMMU) support in kayfabe v3: readiness design for `v3-viommu` **STATUS: DESIGN, revised after adversarial review, 2026-10-04.** It supersedes two things: - the draft of the same name; - once OD-1 is ruled, the "Until it is built" paragraph of `docs/design/V3_VIOMMU.md` (`:70-73`) and the realize check proposed in audit S1-32. Nothing here is built yet. Commit A (§7) builds the interim on `v3-viommu`. **Basis.** Verified against kayfabe `origin/master` **789dee9f**. Between `e4fb0190` and 789dee9f only `docs/OWNER_RULINGS.md`, `docs/OWNER_QUESTIONS_2026-10-03.md` and the stage-1 audit changed, so every code line cited here holds at both commits. Other sources: - QEMU: `/workspace/bench/qemu-10.2.4`. - Open GPU kernel modules: ogkm 580.159.04, abbreviated `ogkm`. - Linux: `research_clones/linux`, 7.1-rc6. Citations I did not re-read myself carry **(lens)**. Behaviour of closed firmware or Windows is UNVERIFIED unless sourced. **What the review changed, in short:** 1. amd-iommu with its default `dma-remap=off` was **fail-open** under the draft. It is now refused by name as `UNTRACKED`. 2. The default regime and the classifier are now **fail-closed**: `UNSET` and `BLOCKED` both refuse. 3. The UNMAP fast path had a TOCTOU hole. It is fixed with a shadow generation, and the notifier always enqueues. 4. The seam's compile-time guarantee is stated honestly: it arrives only at Tier 3. 5. Device addresses are typed at the decode sites, not at the consumers. 6. Three unlisted DMA-address sites were added. 7. The collision map is corrected. 8. Wrong claims are fixed: the virtio-iommu strict claim, the "no identity flash" claim and the thread claim. 9. Two detection lags are recorded: intel `caching-mode=off`, and AMD clearing IOMMUEN at runtime. **Governing rulings.** - §Q, last bullet (`docs/OWNER_RULINGS.md:487-491`): *"A guest DMA address (an IOVA under a guest vIOMMU) is a fourth kind. It must be translated to a GPA at one validated boundary before any of the rules above apply."* - §Q owner text, verbatim: *"Gpga offsets can't, outside guest vram is invalid. Gpa offset can't either, only reference guest ram or its bar or an error. Same for bar offsets. Passthrough uses a sandboxed channel, that strictly only maps based on pte/pdb and nothing else. Translated uses a channel only gpga and/or gpa is mapped."* - On host-process addresses, also verbatim: *"only for the cuda channel (vmm ptx refresher), and this offset is never supplied or given by guest."* - §A.4: no blocking on a vCPU. The only exception is a PRAMIN window move. - §A.9: in-guest isolation matters. - §R: the `_unsafe` perimeter. - 2026-09-25 (`V3_VIOMMU.md` STATUS): a vIOMMU is a **compatibility** requirement, needed to support any stock OS. --- ## 1. Answer: guest IOVAs are not supported today, and they are not refused either - **Nothing in the code path knows a vIOMMU exists.** kf3 learns guest RAM from a single MemoryListener on `address_space_memory` (`qemu/hw/misc/kf3/kf3.c:909-916`). It never asks QEMU for the device's DMA address space. The `iommu`/`iova` matches under `crates/`, `qemu/` and `cuda/` are prose about the *host* (`kf-abi/src/bringup.rs:792,799`) and NVDisplay constant names. - **Every guest-programmed sysmem address is treated as a GPA.** All of them reach `RamMap::block_for` / `RamMap::file_range` (`crates/kf-qemu/src/mem.rs:103-115, 139-143`). There are exactly **13 call sites**, verified by grep: - `chan.rs:518, 801, 2751, 2773, 3187` - `device.rs:747, 2605, 2618` - `display.rs:1064, 1094, 1122, 1170` - `mem.rs:1611` The guest driver programs these addresses with `memdescGetPhysAddr(…, AT_GPU)`. Under an IOMMU mapping that call returns the `iovaArray` (ogkm `mem_desc.c:3305-3324`). - **The refusal the docs describe does not exist.** - `THE_DESIGN.md` §9.4 (`:1160-1166`) says *"A guest IOMMU is detected and refused at device realize."* - `THE_OPEN_QUESTIONS.md:41` lists the same refusal. - Neither is built: audit **S1-32** is open (`docs/audits/2026-10-03-v3-stage1.md:658-668`), and `V3_VIOMMU.md:70-73` itself says "Not built either". - The pre-v3 tree had a CI "GPA-accessor gate" that funnelled guest-physical access through one site. It was removed at the 2026-09-26 archive move (`scripts/ci_gates.sh:93-96`), and v3 has nothing in its place. ### 1.1 What happens today when the guest translates kf3's DMA This is predicted from source, not measured. **Where the IOVAs land.** 1. Linux allocates PCI IOVAs below 4 GiB first, top-down (`linux drivers/iommu/dma-iommu.c:791-797`). 2. It reserves the host-bridge MMIO windows out of the IOVA space (`dma-iommu.c:507-523`). 3. q35 puts its PCI hole at end-of-low-RAM (`hw/pci-host/q35.c:508-514`); low RAM ends at `0x80000000` or `0xb0000000` (`hw/i386/pc_q35.c:161-165`) (lens). 4. So early IOVAs fall **inside valid guest RAM**, and a misread IOVA usually resolves silently to an unrelated guest page. 5. Only IOVAs above top-of-RAM, which appear once 32-bit IOVA space is exhausted, are refused today as `NotGuestRam`. **Per-site outcome** (full detail in §2): - **Fake GSP boot** is the first consumer. It reads the LibOS args and RMARGS through the guest-RAM port and gets unrelated pages. The likely outcome is a named `GspFault` (`RmargsRegionAbsent` at `kf-gsp/src/boot.rs:1265, 1419`, or `RegionMalformed`), and the driver load fails. This is inferred. If the garbage happens to parse, the VMM CPU writes status-queue headers and replies into unrelated guest pages. - **Walked sysmem PTE leaves** become host rows over unrelated guest pages, and the host GPU then reads and writes them silently. This includes rows built from unprivileged guest userspace's page tables. That is an **in-guest isolation break (§A.9)**, not only corruption. - **Passthrough USERD and the error notifier** (`chan.rs:2741-2790`): host RM and the host GSP write `GP_GET` and RC records into unrelated pages. - **Translated CE physical operands**: copies hit unrelated pages, or are refused as `Untranslatable` when the range is not contiguous (`kf-chan/src/translated.rs:392, 726-736`). - **Display**: VMM-CPU notifier and semaphore writes, and instance and pushbuffer reads, hit wrong pages (`display.rs:1060-1174`). **Is anything worse than inside the VM? No.** - Every resolution ends in `RamMap`, which holds only real guest RAM. `kf3_is_guest_ram` excludes ROM and ram_device regions (`kf3.c:536-540`), and lookups resolve into the guest's own memfd (`mem.rs:139-143`). - Host channels keep `DENY_PHYSICAL_MODE_CE` (`V3_VIOMMU.md:33-36`). - So the blast radius is the guest's own RAM. Inside the guest, though, the result is silent corruption plus an isolation break, which is more serious than the "minor" rating S1-32 gives it. --- ## 2. Site table (merged, deduplicated, completed) **Cost key:** - **S** = cost with the seam (§3) placed now. - **L** = cost if it is retrofitted later without the seam. | # | Consumer (kayfabe) | Guest source (AT_GPU) | Thread | Under a translating vIOMMU today | With translation (later) | S / L | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | **Walked sysmem leaves → host VAS rows**, both planes.
The walker emits them raw and coalesces by address contiguity (`cuda/walk/kf_walk.cu:488-504`), which under a vIOMMU means IOVA contiguity.
Bound at `kf-mem/src/ledger.rs:78-110`, one call per run (`kf-mem/src/apply.rs:404-421`), closure `kf-qemu/src/device.rs:744-748` → `file_range` | RM sysmem PTEs (ogkm `mem_desc.c:3305-3324`); UVM CPU chunks (`uvm_gpu.c:3722-3751`) | VA manager | Host GPU reads and writes an unrelated guest page; above RAM, `NotGuestRam` | One IOVA-contiguous run becomes k GPA pieces, each ≥ the host grain, placed as **one** placement; unmap by extent; tombstone and re-place on a vIOMMU remap. Walker unchanged | moderate / moderate+ | | 2 | **BAR1/BAR2 window sysmem targets.** Same closure through `kf-mem/src/cpuwin.rs:481-500` → `place_ram` | BAR PTEs (AT_GPU) | VA manager | Wrong guest page in the CPU window | Same closure; on UNMAP, re-point to scratch. `V3_VIOMMU.md` §3.4 is wrong here: the window *aperture* is CPU MMIO, but its sysmem *target* is GPU DMA | trivial / moderate | | 3 | **PRAMIN at a sysmem target**, decided on the vCPU: `mem.rs:1699-1712` (plan), `:1608-1612` (closure), `cpuwin.rs:774-783` | `kbusVerifyBar2` sets `_TARGET` from the memdesc aperture (ogkm `kern_bus_gm107.c:4071-4086`) (lens). Pre-Hopper only (`kern_bus_gh100.c:207`) (lens). It serves:

review_issues: FAIL-OPEN (detection): amd-iommu with its default dma-remap=off never enables the IOMMU MR for any device (QEMU amd_iommu.c:1114-1121, 1259-1261, 2340/2385; property default false at :2657). QEMU tells the guest nothing about this: HATDis/HATS-reserved are set only for dma-translation=off (acpi-build.c:1866-1867, amd_iommu.c:120-122). A Linux guest gets DMA domains by default (linux amd/iommu.c:3128-3153), so kf3 receives IOVAs while the proposed listener reads IDENTITY. That is the silent corruption the design set out to stop. §4.1 says this configuration 'works today' and §4.3 lists it under 'works meanwhile'; both statements are wrong for any guest that translates. Fix: at machine-done, a QOM lookup of amd-iommu (dma-remap=false and dma-translation=true) publishes a new UNTRACKED regime, which refuses by name. Remedy for operators: dma-remap=on, or dma-translation=off.

FAIL-OPEN (default and classifier): Commit A's regime cell defaults to Direct (RamMap::default at device.rs:394) until the machine-done notifier fires. Its classifier also maps 'no IOMMU section' to IDENTITY, which covers an address space with no RAM sections at all. Fix: Rust default UNSET, which refuses. IDENTITY only on positive evidence (RAM sections present and no IOMMU section). An address space with neither is BLOCKED, which refuses. Unknown wire values refuse.

FACTUAL (sec. 4.2): 'publishing at commit avoids a false IDENTITY flash' is wrong. memory_region_set_enabled commits each change as its own transaction (memory.c:2731-2740). Every vIOMMU switch flips two regions in two commits: intel_iommu.c:1760-1777, amd_iommu.c:1114-1121, virtio-iommu.c:124-130. So every real transition passes through an intermediate commit with neither region enabled. It is harmless only with the positive classifier above. Other devices' invalidations do not trigger it, because set_enabled returns early when nothing changes.

ORDERING HOLE (sec. 5): the UNMAP fast path ('query reverse index; nothing overlaps, return') races with any consumer that sits between resolving through the shadow and registering in the reverse index. The consumers are the VA thread mid-reconcile, the drainer at twin birth, the worker building a USERD view and a vCPU re-pointing PRAMIN. The result is a host row or binding over an IOVA the guest has already unmapped, with no revocation ever queued. Fix: a shadow generation (seqlock) that consumers re-check after registering, revoking themselves on mismatch. In addition, the notifier always enqueues the UNMAP range to the VA-manager FIFO with one eventfd write, which is the same vCPU budget as invalidate_write (mem.rs:13-14), instead of deciding from the index alone.

SEAM LEAK: both Gpa newtypes have public fields: kf-arch ids.rs:12-16 and :98-101 via id_newtype, and kf-mem addr.rs:13 'pub struct Gpa(pub u64)'. Neither is used by RamMap. DevAddr::raw() is public too, so Gpa(d.raw()) and ram.block_for(d.raw(), n) both compile. The 'no From/Into' rule is a labelling aid, not a boundary. The only compile-time boundary is RamMap's lookups becoming private to the DMA module, and the design defers that to Tier 3, after v3-broker. Until then the guarantee is the runtime gate alone, and the design must say so. v3 already dropped the pre-v3 GPA-accessor gate at the archive move (scripts/ci_gates.sh:93-96); nothing has replaced it.

SEAM PLACEMENT: the decode sites still type device addresses as 'gpa' u64 and document them as guest-physical: kf-abi notifier.rs:270 (ErrorNotifier::Sysmem{gpa}) and :542 (UserdMem::Sysmem{base}), and kf-arch lib.rs:308-311 ('Guest-physical address of the 512-byte slot'). Commit B converts only at the consumers. Convert at the decode sites instead. kf-abi notifier.rs, kf-arch and kf-rm rmgraph.rs are touched by no in-flight branch.

MISSED SITES (not reachable today, but unlisted): (a) the ALLOC_MEMORY RPC pte_desc page arrays. memRegisterWithGsp (ogkm mem.c:483-488, 515-560) feeds _issuePteDescRpc (rpc.c:2252-2302). Its callers are display (disp_common_kern_ctrl_minimal.c:316-327), the profiler PMA (kern_profiler_v2_ctrl.c:299-302), deferred_api.c:371 and FBSR via memdescSendMemDescToGSP (mem_desc.c:4786-4866, AT_GPU page list at :4842-4843). kf3 currently refuses it as RpcFunction::Other (kf-gsp rpc.rs:243). (b) FBSR_INIT sysmemAddrOfSuspendResumeData (fbsr_gm107.c:120-126). (c) The channel's eccErrorNotifierMem, which is decoded but unused. Add all three to the inert/refused row with the DevAddr rule.

FACTUAL (sec. 5): 'Guests then run strict' is false for virtio-iommu. Linux advertises IOMMU_CAP_DEFERRED_FLUSH there (linux drivers/iommu/virtio-iommu.c:1084-1085), so the default domain is DMA-FQ and an UNMAP reaches QEMU only when the flush queue is flushed. Harm stays in the lazy-mode class; correct the text.

DETECTION LAG (intel, caching-mode=off): QEMU switches a pass-through device's address space only on a context invalidation, or lazily on the device's first translate (vtd_pt_enable_fast_path, intel_iommu.c:2184-2200). Linux with CM=0 flushes only the write buffer on a not-present-to-present context change (linux intel/iommu.c:1128-1140). kf3 never translates, so a runtime switch of kf3 to identity is never observed and kf3 stays TRANSLATING. This over-refuses (fail-closed). Boot-time iommu=pt is unaffected, because Linux attaches default domains (:2659) before it enables translation (:2669-2672). Record this. Do not add a probe translate: on a non-PT device it raises guest-visible DMAR faults.

FULL-SUPPORT HOLE (AMD): clearing IOMMUEN at runtime switches no address space (amd_iommu.c:1592-1620), but translate returns identity once the IOMMU is disabled (:1941-1949). A notifier-fed shadow would then go stale and mistranslate. Interim behaviour is fail-closed. Full support must treat this state as UNTRACKED.

COLLISION MAP: chan.rs is not free. v3-dispsw-exp adds about 589 lines (hunks at 50, 85, 962, 1128, 1483, 2258, 2439-2537, 2870, 3681), though none at 509-522, 801, 2741-2790 or 3184-3193. kf-gsp/src/boot.rs is touched by v3-broker (+24) and v3-dispsw-exp (+194). v3-dispsw-exp also touches kf3.c :130 and :794, kf3.h :15 and :40-42, ffi_unsafe.rs :17 and :94-117, and device.rs :50-65, 241-249, 598-671, 868, 2229 and 2881.

THREAD CLAIM (sec. 4.2): the listener's commit callback is global (memory.c:1155-1163). It runs on whichever BQL holder commits any memory transaction in the VM, which includes the main loop, vCPUs and IOThreads, and not only on the vCPU that wrote the vIOMMU register. It must stay O(1): compare and publish only on a change.

LOCK ORDER (sec. 5): the VA thread already waits, bounded, for a main-loop bottom half (kf3.c:370-375). If it holds the shadow or reverse-index lock across that wait, or across any host RM call, it deadlocks against a notifier that runs under the BQL. State the rule: never hold the shadow lock across any wait or syscall.

OWNER MODEL: option (b) derives passthrough rows from PTE composed with the guest's own IOMMU tables. The owner's wording is 'strictly only maps based on pte/pdb and nothing else'. The design should state the invariant explicitly: the vIOMMU can only remove a row or redirect it within guest RAM, never add a row or a window. It should also be put to the owner for confirmation (new OD-6).

INTERIM SUBSTITUTION (not a refusal): under TRANSLATING, a BAR1, BAR2 or PRAMIN page whose sysmem target is refused falls back to per-BAR scratch (cpuwin.rs:776-781, the existing 'never a hole' rule). Guest CPU reads there return scratch contents rather than an error, and writes are discarded. This matches today's unbacked pages; record it and count it.

done: Answer to the owner's question, now in docs/design/V3_VIOMMU.md (STATUS LIVE 2026-10-04): guest IOVAs are not supported. Before this branch they were not refused either: all 13 RamMap call sites read a guest IOVA as a GPA, silently. The realize-time refusal described in THE_DESIGN.md §9.4 and THE_OPEN_QUESTIONS.md was never built.

Commit A (97cadd42 + 70227227), detection and fail-closed interim. kf3.c classifies the device's DMA address space at machine-done; hot-plug classifies at once, and -device order does not matter. Regimes: DIRECT; UNTRACKED for amd-iommu with dma-remap=off (also when two amd-iommus exist or the properties cannot be read); otherwise a MemoryListener decides: any IOMMU section gives TRANSLATING, RAM only gives IDENTITY, neither gives BLOCKED. The C rules live in a new QEMU-free header, qemu/hw/misc/kf3/kf3_dma.h, which CI compiles and runs. Rust side: kf3_dma_regime(h, u32) is one atomic store into kf_arch::dma::DmaRegimeCell, which starts Unset (refusing). An unknown wire value refuses. RamMap::block_for and file_range refuse and count unless the regime is Direct or Identity. The GSP refusal names the regime, and the status line carries dma= and dma_refused=. kf3_instance_finalize disarms the notifier and listener after a failed realize.
KF3_ABI is 15, not 14 as the design said. v3-cand-1's kf3.h reserves 14 for v3-broker merged onto 13.

Commit B (509f590e), the typed seam, behaviour unchanged. kf_arch::dma::DevAddr is now the type at the decode sites: UserdMem::Sysmem.base, ErrorNotifier::Sysmem{at}, walked sysmem leaves, the GSP port and CE physical operands. New kf_mem::dma module: RamPiece, DmaRefusal, the DmaResolve trait, and IdentityFn. desired_from_leaves, ApplyCfg.dma and VaManager::new now take a DmaResolve. LeafRefusal::DeviceAddress replaces NotGuestRam, and a multi-piece run is refused by name. New kf-qemu DmaSpace boundary (mem.rs). It now serves the VA-manager leaves, the GSP port, SlotWindow, the completion probe, passthrough USERD and notifier birth, and the Translated USERD view. kf-harness gates 2-8 and publish.rs wrap their closures in IdentityFn. kf-mem gains a kf-arch dependency (one Cargo.lock line).

Commit C (05009d07), docs. V3_VIOMMU.md carries the full revised design: answer, 18-row site table, seam, detection and interim, sync point, effort, what the branch builds and where it departs from the design, tests with mutations, the 10 box tests, the collision map, OD-1 to OD-6, and an unverified list. The 2026-09-25 text is kept as §P0-§P4, with corrections placed above the passages they correct. Also updated: THE_DESIGN.md §9.4 and the THE_OPEN_QUESTIONS.md row marked SUPERSEDED in their own text; THE_TRANSLATED_PLANE.md corrected; audit S1-32 status, rejected check, severity note and table row 29.

Mutations: 23 applied, and every one made the named tests fail. Commit A: M1-M14 plus M9b and M11b, re-run because M9 and M11 had only failed by not compiling under -Werror. Commit B: MB1-MB7. All are listed in the commit messages and in V3_VIOMMU.md §7.4.

Trial merges (git merge-tree) with v3-broker 34696441, v3-cand-1 8a682f1b and v3-dispsw-exp 86b4fa10 conflict only on the KF3_ABI lines in kf3.h and ffi_unsafe.rs. v3-sec-nonpriv, v3-sec-p0 and v3-scratch-bound have the same conflicts against master alone. v3-sec-rawaddr (e4fb0190) is already in master. Nothing was changed in kf-cuda, display.rs, kf-gsp/boot.rs, kf-host or kf-linux-raw.
not_done: The PRAMIN sysmem target (PraminPool closure in kf-mem/src/cpuwin.rs and its construction in kf-qemu/src/mem.rs) is not on DmaSpace. v3-cand-1, which the design's collision map does not list, reworks exactly those lines, so moving them now would certainly conflict. The PRAMIN refusing-resolver unit test waits with it. PRAMIN is still covered by Commit A's runtime gate.

Tier 3 is not done, by design: display.rs x4 waits for v3-broker to merge, and RamMap lookups are not yet private and there is no compile-fail test. Until then the guarantee is the runtime gate plus review; DevAddr::translator_raw is public.
The translator itself (§5: notifier-fed shadow with generation, reverse index, revocation, k-piece placement) is not built. The design estimates ~16-24 engineer-days.

No box was used. The 10 box tests in V3_VIOMMU.md §7.5 are written down but not run, kf3.c has not been compiled or linked for real, and nothing about the listener's behaviour against a real vIOMMU has been run.
The audit S1-32 heading still says minor and §1's severity counts are unchanged. The body records that it reads as major on the audit's scale and leaves the re-rating to the audit's next revision.

Deviation from instructions: the local cargo target was /data/claude-kf-tgt-viommu, not /tmp/claude-0/kf-tgt-viommu, because / had only 4.2 GB free at the start. It has been deleted. / is now at 2.3 GB free because of other processes; nothing of mine is left there except the worktree, which is about 270 MB.
owner_decisions: OD-1: refuse at use (regime classified at machine-done) instead of refusing at realize as S1-32 proposed. This is built that way on v3-viommu.
OD-2: how the vIOMMU-invalidation sync point behaves. Options: async revocation with an overlap counter (recommended now); deferred completion through a QEMU vIOMMU patch; or an exception to §A.4.

OD-3: require MAP-capable vIOMMU configurations (intel caching-mode=on, snoop-control=off, x-flts=off; amd dma-remap=on; virtio-iommu), and refuse SMMUv3, UNMAP-only setups and AMD with IOMMUEN off by name.
OD-4: document bypass_iommu / dma-translation=off as the zero-code answer for guests that need a vIOMMU only for interrupt remapping. Such guests get no DMA confinement for kf3.
OD-5: refuse amd-iommu dma-remap=off (QEMU's default) as UNTRACKED. This is built that way. It also refuses iommu=pt guests in that configuration; their remedy is dma-remap=on or dma-translation=off.

OD-6: confirm that combining passthrough rows with the guest's own IOMMU table satisfies "strictly only maps based on pte/pdb and nothing else". That combination can only remove a row or redirect it within guest RAM, never add a row or a window.
Raise S1-32 from minor to major? This changes the audit heading and its §1 counts.
Confirm KF3_ABI 15 for this surface. Distinct numbers are needed: 12 broker, 13 dispsw-exp, 14 reserved by v3-cand-1 for broker-on-13. The merger re-numbers whichever lands later.
